name: Polo
energy: Repeated hard efforts in 7-minute chukkas with short breaks: elite riders average about 150 bpm in a match, so an aerobic base with repeat-effort fitness matters.
summary: Polo needs a strong trunk, adductors and legs to stay in the saddle while riding off and swinging, and injuries are rare but often serious, mostly from falls. The plan builds rotation, trunk and groin capacity, hitting-arm forearm and shoulder strength, and neck strength.

evidence.claim: In 103 polo riders, 40% were injured over two years and two thirds of injuries kept them out for more than 30 days; falls from the horse caused 44%, and the wrist and low back were the most common overuse pain sites.
evidence.source: Neumayr & Schmitt 2019, German Journal of Sports Medicine

evidence.claim: In Argentine high goal polo, injuries occurred at 7.8 per 1,000 player-game hours, with arms, legs and head most affected and fractures from falls the most common type.
evidence.source: Costa-Paz, Aponte-Tinao & Muscolo 1999, British Journal of Sports Medicine

evidence.claim: Elite polo players averaged 150 bpm across a match and spent most playing time in the hard heart rate zone.
evidence.source: Wright & Peters 2008, International Journal of Performance Analysis in Sport

variants.name: Field polo
variants.desc: Four a side on a big field at high speed, with long swings and many pony changes.
variants.note: Standard plan: rotation, trunk and hitting-arm work.

variants.name: Arena polo
variants.desc: Three a side in an enclosed arena with more riding off and short, quick play, usually in winter.
variants.note: More adductor and trunk bracing for riding off; the winter season shifts your in-season block.

variants.name: Back (No. 4)
variants.desc: Defensive role with more riding off and backhand shots.
variants.note: Train rotation to both sides and extra adductor work.

off.name: Lower and groin strength
off.focus: Legs, adductors and back for the saddle

slots.note: Build over weeks; groin pain is common in polo.
Wall sit high, like standing in the stirrups.

off.name: Rotation and upper
off.focus: Swing power, pulling and hitting-arm forearm

slots.note: Hitting arm wrist and forearm; both arms.

in.name: Strength upkeep
in.focus: Short full body early in the week

in.name: Trunk and prehab
in.focus: Back, neck, forearm; no heavy legs

off.name: Aerobic base
off.intensity: 85-95% max heart rate, hard but steady
off.why: Builds the base for repeated hard chukkas.

off.name: Steady cardio
off.why: Recovery and base when not riding.

pre.name: Chukka intervals
pre.work: 4 x 7 min of 20 s hard / 40 s easy
pre.why: Mimics 7-minute chukkas with 3-minute pony changes; practice.

tests.name: Copenhagen plank hold
tests.how: Top leg on a bench at the knee (short lever), time per side

tests.name: Side plank hold
tests.how: Forearm and feet, straight line, each side

tests.name: Rotational med ball throw
tests.how: 3 kg ball, side-on throw for distance, best of 3 each side
tests.note: No polo norms. Keep sides within 10-15%.

tests.name: Two-point wall sit
tests.how: Back on wall, knees about 120 degrees, like standing in stirrups

week: Matches at the weekend: lower and groin session Monday or Tuesday.
Trunk, neck and upper session midweek.
No heavy legs within 72 h of a match.
Stick and ball and riding count as training; cut gym if riding several ponies a day.
primer: Dynamic hip and trunk warm-up, 5 min
Med ball rotational throws 2 x 3 per side
Neck isometrics 1 x 10 s each way

lines: Cut gym volume by half, keep loads.
Keep stick and ball sharp and short.

rules: Wear a helmet that meets the current standard and use face protection.
Suspected concussion: off at once and no return to play for at least 21 days (HPA rule since 2023).
Groin pain: reduce riding off and Copenhagen load, then rebuild; do not play through it.
Train rotation to both sides, not only the hitting side.

sources.source: Neumayr & Schmitt 2019, German Journal of Sports Medicine
Costa-Paz, Aponte-Tinao & Muscolo 1999, British Journal of Sports Medicine
Wright & Peters 2008, International Journal of Performance Analysis in Sport
Ham Polo Club, Rules of polo
